title: Cross-account access with an IAM role
claim: Two policies on the role are checked: the trust policy when the user assumes the role, and the permissions policy when the role reads the bucket.
alt: A sequence with three actors: a user in account A, AWS STS, and a bucket in account B. The user calls AssumeRole on AWS STS and names a role in account B. AWS STS checks the trust policy of the role and returns temporary credentials to the user. The user then sends a GetObject request to the bucket. Amazon S3 checks the permissions policy of the role.
notes: Pilot for the diagram gate. Redrawn on 2026-10-04 after the pilot gate as a sequence, because the exchange is ordered in time: every arrow is now a request or a response, and each policy check is a highlighted note on the lifeline of the service that makes it (a check drawn as a message from a service to itself made the figure too wide for a phone). Not checked against the fact canon. Not drawn: the identity-based policy in account A that lets the user call AssumeRole, and the bucket policy. A chapter figure must say in the prose whether those are needed, from the canon.

messages.label: AssumeRole
messages.say: The IAM user in account A calls AssumeRole on AWS STS and names the role in account B, and AWS STS checks the trust policy of the role.

messages.label: Credentials
messages.say: The trust policy names account A as a trusted principal, so AWS STS returns temporary security credentials for the role.

messages.label: GetObject
messages.say: The user signs a GetObject request with the temporary credentials, and Amazon S3 checks the permissions policy of the role.
